section: 73rd Amendment - Part IX, Eleventh Schedule, three-tier structure, Gram Sabha, reservations, State Election Commission
subsections: Tier structure and membership - population exemption, age, elections, tenure, dissolution
Gram Sabha - definition, composition, functions, People's Plan Campaign, PESA powers
States and areas exempted from Part IX and the 74th Amendment; extension through PESA

accepted.s: Under Article 243B of the Constitution, which of the following is the correct three-tier structure of Panchayats?
accepted.x: Article 243B provides for Panchayats at the village, intermediate and district levels.
accepted.tq: Directly identify the constitutional structure from the three levels.
accepted.sec: Tier structure and membership - population exemption, age, elections, tenure, dissolution  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A State having a population not exceeding 20 lakh may constitutionally dispense with which tier of Panchayati Raj institutions?
accepted.x: Article 243B permits a State with a population not exceeding 20 lakh to omit the intermediate level of Panchayats.
accepted.tq: Use the population threshold to distinguish the optional intermediate tier.
accepted.sec: Tier structure and membership - population exemption, age, elections, tenure, dissolution  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The minimum age prescribed for becoming a member of a Panchayat is:
accepted.x: Article 243F prescribes 21 years as the minimum age for membership of a Panchayat.
accepted.tq: Numerical age questions require separating Panchayat membership from voting age.
accepted.sec: Tier structure and membership - population exemption, age, elections, tenure, dissolution  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding membership of Panchayats:
1. All members at the three levels are directly elected from territorial constituencies.
2. The Constitution itself prescribes a uniform method for choosing every village chairperson.
3. Chairpersons at the intermediate and district levels are elected by and from among the elected members.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The method of choosing a village chairperson is left to State law; the Constitution does not prescribe one uniform method.
accepted.tq: Split the options by checking the constitutional distinction between members and chairpersons.
accepted.sec: Tier structure and membership - population exemption, age, elections, tenure, dissolution  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the election of chairpersons in Panchayats?
o: All chairpersons are directly elected under Article 243C.
Village chairpersons are elected indirectly and the other two chairpersons are directly elected.
All chairpersons are nominated by the Governor.
Village chairpersons are chosen as State law provides, while intermediate and district chairpersons are elected indirectly.
accepted.x: Article 243C leaves the method of choosing the village chairperson to State law and provides indirect election of intermediate and district chairpersons by and from elected members.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between direct election of members and indirect election of higher-level chairpersons.
accepted.sec: Tier structure and membership - population exemption, age, elections, tenure, dissolution  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The normal constitutional term of a Panchayat is:
accepted.x: A Panchayat ordinarily continues for five years from the date appointed for its first meeting.
accepted.tq: Directly recall the fixed tenure and avoid confusing it with the period for holding fresh elections.
accepted.sec: Tier structure and membership - population exemption, age, elections, tenure, dissolution  [APPSC]

accepted.s: If a Panchayat is dissolved before the expiry of its normal term, elections to reconstitute it shall ordinarily be completed within:
o: The remaining period of the original term only
accepted.x: Elections must ordinarily be completed within six months of dissolution. No election is necessary when the remainder of the Panchayat's term is less than six months.
accepted.tq: Separate the six-month election deadline from the exception concerning the remaining term.
accepted.sec: Tier structure and membership - population exemption, age, elections, tenure, dissolution  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A Panchayat reconstituted after premature dissolution serves:
o: A fresh full term of five years in every case
A term of six months only
A term fixed by the Election Commission of India
Only the remainder of the term for which the dissolved Panchayat would have continued
accepted.x: The reconstituted Panchayat continues only for the remainder of the original term, not for a fresh five-year period.
accepted.tq: Apply the tenure rule to a premature-dissolution situation.
accepted.sec: Tier structure and membership - population exemption, age, elections, tenure, dissolution  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In Andhra Pradesh, which of the following correctly represents the three Panchayati Raj tiers?
o: Gram Panchayat, Mandal Parishad and Zilla Parishad
Gram Sabha, Municipal Council and Zilla Parishad
Village Council, Taluk Board and District Council
Gram Panchayat, Nagar Panchayat and Zilla Parishad
accepted.x: The Andhra Pradesh structure comprises Gram Panchayats, Mandal Parishads or Mandal Praja Parishads, and Zilla Parishads.
accepted.tq: Match the State-specific names with the three constitutional levels.
accepted.sec: Tier structure and membership - population exemption, age, elections, tenure, dissolution  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to the figures cited for Andhra Pradesh, the State has approximately:
o: 15,000 or more Gram Panchayats, 588 mandals and 13 Zilla Parishads
10,000 Gram Panchayats, 488 mandals and 23 Zilla Parishads
5,000 Gram Panchayats, 288 mandals and 13 Zilla Parishads
20,000 or more Gram Panchayats, 688 mandals and 28 Zilla Parishads
accepted.x: The cited figures are approximately 15,000 or more Gram Panchayats, 588 mandals and 13 Zilla Parishads.
accepted.tq: Read the three figures together instead of isolating only one numerical value.
accepted.sec: Tier structure and membership - population exemption, age, elections, tenure, dissolution  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The 13 Zilla Parishads of Andhra Pradesh are being reorganised into how many Zilla Parishads?
accepted.x: The cited reorganisation proposes increasing the number of Zilla Parishads from 13 to 28.
accepted.tq: Test the before-and-after figures in a current-affairs numerical comparison.
accepted.sec: Tier structure and membership - population exemption, age, elections, tenure, dissolution  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Gram Sabha, under Article 243(b), consists of:
o: All persons registered in the electoral rolls of a village within the Panchayat area
All adult residents of the district
All elected members of the Gram Panchayat בלבד
Only the chairperson and ward members of the village
accepted.x: Article 243(b) defines the Gram Sabha as the body of persons registered in the electoral rolls of a village within the Panchayat area.
accepted.tq: Use the exact constitutional phrase concerning registration in electoral rolls.
accepted.sec: Gram Sabha - definition, composition, functions, People's Plan Campaign, PESA powers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which Article provides for the Gram Sabha to exercise such powers and perform such functions at the village level as the State Legislature may provide by law?
accepted.x: Article 243A deals with the powers and functions of the Gram Sabha, while Article 243(b) defines its composition.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the definition provision and the functions provision.
accepted.sec: Gram Sabha - definition, composition, functions, People's Plan Campaign, PESA powers  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Gram Sabha:
1. Its powers are exhaustively specified by the Constitution and cannot be enlarged by State law.
2. It comprises persons registered in the electoral rolls of villages within the Panchayat area.
3. The State Legislature may confer powers and functions on it by law.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. The Constitution leaves the detailed powers and functions of the Gram Sabha to State legislation, so statement 1 is false.
accepted.tq: Identify the false absolute statement about powers being exhaustively fixed by the Constitution.
accepted.sec: Gram Sabha - definition, composition, functions, People's Plan Campaign, PESA powers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The People's Plan Campaign known as “Sabki Yojana Sabka Vikas” is associated with the preparation of:
accepted.x: The campaign facilitates preparation of Gram Panchayat Development Plans through Gram Sabhas.
accepted.tq: Link the campaign title with its specific planning output.
accepted.sec: Gram Sabha - definition, composition, functions, People's Plan Campaign, PESA powers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: “Sabki Yojana Sabka Vikas” was launched from:
accepted.x: The People's Plan Campaign is stated to have commenced from 2 October 2018.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact launch date rather than the associated national occasions generally used as distractors.
accepted.sec: Gram Sabha - definition, composition, functions, People's Plan Campaign, PESA powers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Gram Panchayat Development Plans primarily aim at:
o: Economic development and social justice at the Gram Panchayat level
accepted.x: GPDPs are plans at the Gram Panchayat level for economic development and social justice.
accepted.tq: Apply the purpose of GPDPs to identify the appropriate planning objective.
accepted.sec: Gram Sabha - definition, composition, functions, People's Plan Campaign, PESA powers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Gram Panchayat Development Plan has been described as an ICT initiative of which Ministry?
o: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
accepted.x: The GPDP was rolled out as an ICT initiative of the Ministry of Panchayati Raj.
accepted.tq: Use the implementing ministry as the deciding clue in a body-function question.
accepted.sec: Gram Sabha - definition, composition, functions, People's Plan Campaign, PESA powers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 is commonly known as:
accepted.x: The Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 is abbreviated as PESA.
accepted.tq: Directly identify the official abbreviation of the legislation.
accepted.sec: Gram Sabha - definition, composition, functions, People's Plan Campaign, PESA powers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: PESA, 1996 was enacted following the recommendations of which committee?
accepted.x: PESA followed the recommendations of the Bhuria Committee, constituted in 1995.
accepted.tq: Avoid the common committee-name trap by linking PESA with the Bhuria Committee.
accepted.sec: Gram Sabha - definition, composition, functions, People's Plan Campaign, PESA powers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: PESA, 1996 extends Part IX of the Constitution to:
o: Fifth Schedule Scheduled Areas, with modifications
All Sixth Schedule areas without exception
accepted.x: Parliament may extend Part IX to Fifth Schedule Scheduled Areas with modifications, and PESA performs this function.
accepted.tq: Distinguish Fifth Schedule Scheduled Areas from Sixth Schedule tribal areas.
accepted.sec: States and areas exempted from Part IX and the 74th Amendment; extension through PESA  [APPSC]

accepted.s: PESA extends Part IX to Scheduled Areas in how many States, as stated in the material?
accepted.x: PESA is stated to extend Part IX to Fifth Schedule areas in ten States, including Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Test the exact number and avoid replacing it with the broader number of tribal-population States.
accepted.sec: Gram Sabha - definition, composition, functions, People's Plan Campaign, PESA powers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a power associated with the Gram Sabha in Scheduled Areas under PESA?
o: Control over village markets and liquor
Compulsory approval of every Union Budget expenditure
Protection of traditions and community resources
accepted.x: PESA gives Gram Sabhas powers over minor forest produce, village markets and liquor, and protection of traditions and community resources; it does not give them control over the Union Budget.
accepted.tq: Find the one unrelated power among the PESA-specific Gram Sabha functions.
accepted.sec: Gram Sabha - definition, composition, functions, People's Plan Campaign, PESA powers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In Scheduled Areas, the Gram Sabha under PESA must be consulted before:
accepted.x: PESA requires consultation with the Gram Sabha before land acquisition in Scheduled Areas.
accepted.tq: Apply the consultation requirement to a land-related administrative decision.
accepted.sec: Gram Sabha - definition, composition, functions, People's Plan Campaign, PESA powers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following functions is specifically associated with the Gram Sabha under PESA in Scheduled Areas?
o: Conducting elections to the Rajya Sabha
Appointing members of the Supreme Court
accepted.x: The Gram Sabha approves local plans and identifies beneficiaries under the enhanced PESA framework.
accepted.tq: Identify the grassroots planning and beneficiary-selection function from the PESA powers.
accepted.sec: Gram Sabha - definition, composition, functions, People's Plan Campaign, PESA powers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states the position of the Gram Sabha in PESA areas?
o: It has only an advisory role in all matters.
It functions exclusively under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
It is subordinate to every customary village institution.
It is regarded as the supreme authority at the village level and may settle disputes according to customary practice.
accepted.x: In PESA areas, the Gram Sabha is regarded as supreme at the village level, protects traditions and may settle disputes according to customary practices.
accepted.tq: Use the institutional-status clue to distinguish enhanced PESA authority from ordinary Gram Sabha powers.
accepted.sec: Gram Sabha - definition, composition, functions, People's Plan Campaign, PESA powers  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Part IX of the Constitution:
1. It does not apply to Nagaland, Meghalaya and Mizoram.
2. It does not apply to Scheduled Areas and tribal areas covered by the Fifth and Sixth Schedules.
3. It does not apply to hill areas of Manipur having District Councils.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements reflect the exemptions specified under Article 243M for Part IX.
accepted.tq: Check each listed constitutional exemption before selecting the inclusive code.
accepted.sec: States and areas exempted from Part IX and the 74th Amendment; extension through PESA  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Part IX is not applicable to which of the following areas in West Bengal?
o: All coastal districts of West Bengal
The entire State of West Bengal
accepted.x: Article 243M excludes the hill council area of Darjeeling district from the application of Part IX.
accepted.tq: Identify the area-specific exemption rather than treating the exclusion as State-wide.
accepted.sec: States and areas exempted from Part IX and the 74th Amendment; extension through PESA  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 243A — Exemption of Sixth Schedule areas from Part IXA
Article 243F — Extension of Part IX through PESA
accepted.x: Article 243M provides exemptions from Part IX. Article 243ZC concerns corresponding exemptions under Part IXA, Article 243A concerns Gram Sabha powers, and Article 243F concerns disqualifications for Panchayat membership.
accepted.tq: Match Articles with their subjects and eliminate swapped provision numbers.
accepted.sec: States and areas exempted from Part IX and the 74th Amendment; extension through PESA  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The parallel constitutional provision concerning exemption from Part IXA, relating to municipalities, is:
accepted.x: Article 243ZC provides the parallel exemption provision for Part IXA, which deals with municipalities and was introduced through the 74th Amendment framework.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Part IX exemption provision from its Part IXA counterpart.
accepted.sec: States and areas exempted from Part IX and the 74th Amendment; extension through PESA  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding reservation of Scheduled Caste seats in Panchayats:
1. SC reservation does not apply in Arunachal Pradesh.
2. The reason is that Arunachal Pradesh has no Scheduled Caste population.
3. This exemption makes Arunachal Pradesh a State to which Part IX does not apply at all.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The absence of SC reservation in Arunachal Pradesh does not mean that Part IX is wholly inapplicable there, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Separate an exemption from a particular reservation from total exclusion of the constitutional Part.
accepted.sec: States and areas exempted from Part IX and the 74th Amendment; extension through PESA  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which Ministry oversees Part IX, PESA and District Planning Committees?
o: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
accepted.x: The Ministry of Panchayati Raj oversees Part IX, PESA and District Planning Committees.
accepted.tq: Identify the responsible ministry by matching it with the cluster of decentralisation functions.
accepted.sec: States and areas exempted from Part IX and the 74th Amendment; extension through PESA  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Ministry of Panchayati Raj was created on:
accepted.x: The Ministry of Panchayati Raj was created on 27 May 2004.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact date associated with the creation of the nodal Ministry.
accepted.sec: States and areas exempted from Part IX and the 74th Amendment; extension through PESA  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following groups correctly identifies the tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram to which Part IX does not apply?
o: Areas notified under the Municipalities Act
accepted.x: Part IX does not apply to tribal areas covered by the Sixth Schedule in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.
accepted.tq: Use the Schedule distinction to identify the constitutional category of exempt tribal areas.
accepted.sec: States and areas exempted from Part IX and the 74th Amendment; extension through PESA  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025, the proposed number of days of employment is:
accepted.x: The VB-G RAM G Act, 2025 is stated to replace MGNREGA and provide 125 days of employment.
accepted.tq: Test the precise employment-days figure in the current policy provision.
accepted.sec: Gram Sabha - definition, composition, functions, People's Plan Campaign, PESA powers  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The VB-G RAM G Act, 2025 links planned works with:
o: PM Gati Shakti through Viksit Gram Panchayat Plans
The National Education Policy through District Education Plans
The Smart Cities Mission through Municipal Development Plans
The Finance Commission through State Annual Plans
accepted.x: The Act is described as planning works through Viksit Gram Panchayat Plans linked to PM Gati Shakti.
accepted.tq: Match the new Act with its distinctive planning framework and linked programme.
accepted.sec: Gram Sabha - definition, composition, functions, People's Plan Campaign, PESA powers  [APPSC]
